The prosecution says 向某指使他人故意伤害他人身体，致一人死亡. So the crime is "故意伤害致死" which under Chinese law is "故意伤害罪" with result death, could be "故意伤害致人死亡" (i.e., "故意伤害致人死亡" is a specific provision). Also there is "指使他人故意伤害" which is "组织、领导、指挥犯罪" maybe "组织、领导、指挥他人实施犯罪" (罪名: 组织、领导、指挥他人实施故意伤害罪). However Chinese criminal law has article 23: "组织、领导、指挥他人实施犯罪的，依照所组织、领导、指挥的犯罪定罪处罚". So if he directed others to commit intentional injury, he can be charged with "组织、领导、指挥故意伤害罪". But typical charge is "故意伤害罪" for the principal, and "帮助犯" maybe. The facts: He instructed Zhang to beat Li, but the death was caused by Zhang stabbing Wang. Did he order that stabbing? Not clear. He directed to beat Li, but the death was caused by a different act (stabbing). However the result is death of Wang due to stabbing by Zhang. The prosecution says "指使他人故意伤害他人身体，致一人死亡". So they treat as "故意伤害致死". So charge: "故意伤害致死". In Chinese naming, they might just list "故意伤害". According to correction rule: When violent altercation where death resulted but no premeditated intent to kill, appropriate charge is intentional injury (故意伤害) and a "致死" aggravating circumstance. So we list "故意伤害". Also maybe "组织、领导、指挥他人故意伤害". But rule says list multiple crimes only when distinct offenses. Here the conduct is指使他人故意伤害, which is a separate offense of "组织、领导、指挥他人犯罪". However Chinese law treats that as a separate crime: "组织、领导、指挥他人实施犯罪" (Article 23). So we could list both: "故意伤害" and "组织、领导、指挥他人故意伤害". But the instruction: "When the factual scenario involves a defendant biting or otherwise assaulting a police officer while resisting law‑enforcement duties, charge only 妨害公务". Not relevant.
